cases.ac: Stone block: clicks 1-2 show crack stages, click 3 removes it and +1 stone inventory; HUD updates.
cases.oracle: Dig a stone (type 3) cell: click 1 leaves the cell present with per-cell damage hits=1 and the crack overlay at its first visible stage; click 2 leaves it present at a strictly deeper second crack stage (visible stages stay within 1..hardness-1 per the pure crack function of (x, y, stage)); click 3 removes the cell, clears its damage entry, and increments stone inventory by exactly 1 with the canvas HUD count updating. A wood (type 4) cell behaves identically. Damage accrues once per cell-entry edge: re-entering the cell adds a hit while holding the pointer inside the same cell adds none.

cases.ac: Grass block: single click removes, +1 grass inventory.
cases.oracle: A grass (type 1) cell is removed by a single click with no crack stage shown, incrementing grass inventory by exactly 1; a dirt (type 2) cell behaves the same because hardness 1 means the first hit reaches hardness: removal, +1 dirt inventory, and no damage entry survives the dig.

cases.ac: Placing from palette decrements that type's inventory and refuses at 0.
cases.oracle: With inventory[type] = n >= 1, placing that type into an empty cell writes the cell and decrements that count by exactly 1 through the single setState edit path that persists; with inventory[type] = 0 the placement attempt is refused before any mutation: the target cell is unchanged, the count stays 0, and the palette swatch for that type is greyed out.

cases.ac: Reload persists both the world and the inventory (localStorage).
cases.oracle: After digging one block and placing one block, the single localStorage key holds one JSON blob deep-equal to the live state as {version: 2, cells, inventory} (world and inventory saved together atomically); re-initializing from that storage (reload) restores world cells and per-type inventory deep-equal to the pre-reload values with the transient damage map reset; with empty storage the game boots to the deterministic default world with an all-zero inventory.

cleanup.environment: Headless node --test run from the repo root; no browser, server, daemon or network connection is started and nothing in the environment persists after the run.
cleanup.data: Tests run against an injected in-memory storage double for the localStorage contract; real localStorage, user profiles and repo files are never written; any temp fixture lives in a unique tmp directory and is removed in finally.
